_note: TEACHES DEFENDING GROUND. The campaign's only real duel: the opponent attacks, and
this is the one mission a player can LOSE to somebody other than themselves.
RE-AUTHORED 2026-09-07 to the owner's spec, which was five things: seed 207152, a board
with room for three players seating two, the dragon and the enemy both across the river,
an easy AI, and a visible 'destroy the enemy' objective under the ordinary conquest rule.
⚠️ 'LAST MAN STANDING WITH AN OBJECTIVE ON SCREEN' IS REFUSED AT LOAD, AND THAT IS WHY
THIS FILE SAYS `scenario`. The owner asked for the objective to READ 'destroy the enemy
0/1' and for the WIN to be 'standard last man standing'. `ScenarioDef._read_objectives`
refuses that combination outright -- `mode 'last_man_standing' is decided by conquest, so
its objectives would never be read` -- and it is right to: `ObjectiveSystem` returns early
outside SCENARIO mode, so the rows would have been dead text and the tracker would have
shown 0/1 for the whole match and never ticked. Its refusal message names the fix, and
this file takes it: mode `scenario`, with win rows that ARE the conquest condition.
SO THE RULE IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE. Own nothing and you are out is still the loss on
every map in this game (`ScenarioDef` decision 5), `_scenario` keeps it, and the win is
now 'the enemy has no units and no buildings' -- which is what last man standing means in
a two-player match, said in the vocabulary that can also be drawn on screen.
⚠️ TWO ROWS AND NOT ONE, AND A SINGLE ROW WOULD HAVE BEEN A DIFFERENT MISSION. The
obvious reading of 'destroy the enemy 0/1' is one row -- PLAN.md 11.8's own *leave the
enemy nothing*, `{subject: unit, owner: enemy, == 0}`. That row wins the match on the tick
the enemy's LAST UNIT dies, with their town centre untouched and standing. Worse, a win row
LATCHES (`ObjectiveSystem`'s header): the AI would have retrained a villager the very next
tick, and the player would have won anyway, having razed nothing. Two ANDed rows are
conquest; one row is 'kill their army'. This is scenario 4's shape and its reasoning --
multiple win rows are ANDed, and the half a player finishes first is written out so the
tracker has something to tick early.
A BUILDING COUNTS ONLY WHEN COMPLETE (`ObjectiveSystem._census`), so an enemy reduced to a
lone FOUNDATION satisfies the buildings row while `WinConditionSystem._owns_anything`
would still call them standing. The objective therefore fires a moment EARLIER than pure
conquest in that one case. Left alone deliberately: it is the forgiving direction, and the
alternative is a player hunting the map for a half-built hut.
THE MOTHER DRAGON COUNTS FOR NEITHER ROW, and that is not luck. `owner: enemy` is resolved
from `SimWorld.players`, which gaia has no row in (`ObjectiveSystem` trap 1), so she is in
no owner set at all. Killing her is optional and always was; the win is about the enemy.
⚠️ EVERY WALL, GATE AND TOWER IN THIS GAME NEEDS AGE 2, AND THIS SCENARIO OPENS IN AGE 1.
Checked in buildings.json rather than assumed: `building.wall_wood_short` is
`age_required: 2`, every gate is 2 or higher, `building.watch_tower` is 2 and
`building.guard_tower` is 3. There is NOTHING defensive a player can build in age 1. The
owner asked the briefing to 'recommend building walls and gates and towers at the river
passings', so the briefing SEQUENCES it -- advance first, then fortify -- rather than
recommending four buildings the build menu will not offer for the first several minutes.
That is this card's own trap at full size: a briefing that promises what the rule does not
deliver is indistinguishable, from the player's chair, from a broken game.
📝 `starting_age` IS STILL 1 AND IS THE ONE THING WORTH A SECOND OPINION. It was not in
the owner's list, so it was left where it was, and it makes this the campaign's capstone:
scenario 1 taught the economy, 2 the age ladder, 3 the fight, 4 the dragon, and 5 asks for
all of it under pressure. The alternative is `starting_age: 2`, which puts walls, gates and
watch towers in the build menu from the first second and makes the owner's sentence read
literally. It is ONE FIELD and needs no re-authoring -- the map does not depend on the age.
THE BRIEFING NAMES THE GATE MECHANIC ON PURPOSE. A gate is `buildable: false` and is
reached by upgrading a finished LONG wall (5.3/5.8), so a player told to 'build gates' will
look in the build menu and not find one. The owner confirmed that upgrade path in play on
2026-09-07, which is what makes it safe to teach here.
name: How To Survive the Initial Attack and Defeat the Enemy
description: One enemy, one river, and one ford between you. They will attack. Hold the crossing, then take their land.
message:
Objective: Destroy the enemy.

Overview: One enemy shares this valley with you, and they will come for you. This is a true duel -- the opponent attacks, and this is a mission you can lose.

The river splits the valley in two, and there is exactly ONE way across it on foot: a sand ford at the very centre of the map. That ford is the only road an army has into your half, and holding it is the whole of your defence.

Walls, gates and watch towers all arrive with the Age of Embers, so advance as soon as you can afford it and then fortify the crossing. A gate is not in the build menu -- drag a LONG wall, tap it, and upgrade it into a gate. That is how you keep a door to march out through.

And something else lives across the water. A dragon guards her nest on the far bank, deep in the enemy's half, and she belongs to nobody. Kill her, hold her nest for six minutes, and her hatchling grows into your dragon. She is not the mission -- the enemy is -- but she is yours if you can take her.
_note_map: THE MAP IS THE SAVED map.png BESIDE THIS FILE (2.4c, PLAN.md 11.3). `seed` is PROVENANCE
ONLY -- `build_config()` never calls MapGenerator, so a generator change cannot move the
ford or the nest this mission is authored around.
112x112, TWO PLAYERS ON ROOM FOR THREE, which is the owner's own lobby configuration:
*'map size 3 payer Player1 + AI, slot 3 closed'*, and their screenshot reads 'River, 112 x
112 - 2 players on room for 3'. `MapGenerator.generate`'s fourth parameter is exactly that
-- `size_players` sizes the board while `players` lays out the starts -- and
`preview_author_maps.ROOM_FOR` is where this scenario asks for it. `data.meta` records both
(`players: 2`, `size_players: 3`), so the sidecar says what happened.
⚠️ ROOM IS NOT A THIRD OPPONENT. Padding `opponents` to widen the board would seat a third
player with a base and an army in a mission authored as a duel. There are two starts on
this map and there is no third base to find.
EVERY FIGURE BELOW IS MEASURED OFF THE FILE -- entities out of map.json, terrain out of
map.png's R channel, which is the only channel that is data:
board            112 x 112, 163 entities, 2 starts
terrain          82.2% grass, 12.5% shallow water, 5.3% sand. NO DEEP WATER AT ALL
player 1 start   (56, 85)   town centre (51, 80)
player 2 start   (56, 26)   town centre (51, 21)
the river        a diagonal band on x = y, 15 tiles wide (x - y from -7 to +7)
the ford         ONE crossing, at the board's centre: 53 land tiles inside the band,
x 51..61 by y 51..61, all sand but for 8 grass
walk to the ford player 1: 29 tiles.  player 2: 30 tiles.  Symmetric on purpose
the nest         origin (68, 42), CENTRE (73, 47) -- gaia's
the mother       (67, 41) -- gaia's, one of her, 600 hp, flies
THE ENEMY AND THE DRAGON ARE BOTH ACROSS THE WATER, which is the owner's description and
is confirmed by arithmetic rather than by looking at the minimap: x - y is -29 at player
1's start and +30 at player 2's, so they are on opposite sides of a band that runs from -7
to +7; the nest centre is at +26, on player 2's side.
'ONLY ONE WAY ACROSS ON FOOT' IS EXACT, AND THE QUALIFIER IS EARNED. The river is entirely
SHALLOW water -- there is no deep water on this board -- so it is impassable to the LAND
domain and perfectly passable to ships. The AI walks, has no transport rule and will use
the ford; a player who builds a dock can cross wherever they like. The briefing says 'on
foot' so it stays true for both.
⚠️ THE FORD IS OUTSIDE THE MOTHER'S REACH, and it had to be checked because the briefing
sends the player to stand there. Her `aggro_radius` is 10 and it is measured from her POST
-- the nest, not from her (`UnitDef.guards_post`, 13.2a) -- and the nest centre is 19.2
tiles from the middle of the ford. She also clears both starts: 27.0 from player 2's and
41.6 from player 1's, against `nest_start_clearance()`'s floor of 24. So a player walling
the crossing is never fighting a dragon they were not told about.
SHE IS FOUR TIMES CLOSER TO THE ENEMY THAN TO THE PLAYER (27.0 against 41.6 -- nearer in
the ratio that matters, which is who has to cross a river to reach her). Claiming her means
taking ground on the far bank, so the dragon is a reward for winning the crossing rather
than a free 600 hp neighbour.
⚠️ THIS IS THE FIRST PLACE IN THE CAMPAIGN A CLAIMED DRAGON CAN ACTUALLY BE FLOWN, and it
closes a gap card #67 opened. Scenario 4's win row is *own 1 dragon*, so that mission ENDS
on the tick the claim completes -- you are handed a dragon and the victory screen together.
Here the win is about the enemy, so a player who claims her keeps playing and can fly her
at them. It is therefore also the only mission in which the FIRE BREATH (13.4) can be seen,
which is what the owner wanted scenario 5 for.
